svg.text: Store Topology Analyzer — CCC Topology Optimizer · Architecture

Python decision-support app: two front-ends (CLI run.py + a Streamlit web app) driving ONE shared topology_engine · CAIA constraint-aware auto store selection · what-if planning · Excel with live formulas + interactive maps.
Python modules & functions shown as boxes (not classes). Both front-ends contain NO business logic — they only gather input and call the engine.
Layer colour coding (consistent across all views)
Folders named for what they do. Colours match the module boxes & runtime nodes.
Web: cd frontend && py -m streamlit run app.py
Both paths call the same topology_engine, so results always agree.
2 · Layered modules — two front-ends, one engine, a what-if layer
The CLI and the Streamlit web app both only gather input and call topology_engine; utils/state keeps the web run byte-identical to the CLI.
app.py: page config, init_session_state, sidebar status
only gathers input + shows output — no business logic
web reads the SAME bytes as the CLI
CLI flags override YAML; nothing hard-coded
tunable constants used across the engine
raw matrix → one row per CCC with
aggregates OPD per CCC; fuzzy column names
no intermediate file — feeds the optimizer directly
whatif_planning — scenario modeling (reuses the same ranked data + optimizer)
engine.py ScenarioEngine.run_scenario() / compare_scenarios() — orchestrates one or many scenarios
coverage.py served-demand curves gap_detector.py demand-weighted clusters of under-served CCCs
placement.py where a new store helps most what_if.py add / move a store, then re-optimize the whole topology
comparison.py rank scenarios history.py snapshots store_locations.py resolve lat/lng export.py Excel + maps
config.py: scenario config + result dataclasses (coverage %, per-store metrics, gap regions, recommendations)
answers "which stores should we operate, and where are the gaps?" — without changing the core engine
(+ pywin32 for live-formula Excel on Windows)
engine falls back to a built-in k-medoids if sklearn is absent
In: Excel .xlsx / .xlsm (raw distance matrix OR pre-ranked pivot) · GeoJSON / GPKG / SHP (map geo) · YAML config & scenarios · JSON changes
Out: *_optimized.xlsx (Output sheet + Store Scorecards Summary + Uncovered CCCs) · *_map.html (static) · *_interactive.html (click-to-reassign)
auto-versioned outputs (_v2, _v3, …) so nothing is overwritten · all data stays on the local machine (no server, no database)
3 · Runtime / data flow — Excel → detect & rank → select stores → two-pass optimize → Excel + maps
what-if reuses the ranked data + optimizer
Read it as: ① a front-end loads the Excel → ② the engine auto-detects the format and ranks it if raw → ③ you pick preferred stores or let CAIA choose → ④ the optimizer runs the two-pass
assignment and scores each store → ⑤ it writes an Excel workbook (with live formulas) plus static and click-to-reassign maps. The what-if layer branches off the same ranked data.
One local Python process — no server or database. The only "services" are files on disk; the CLI and web app produce identical results because they share the engine.
4 · Trace — the web workflow in auto (CAIA) mode

g.text: Upload — drop the Excel; utils/state writes it to a temp file (identical bytes to the CLI); ranker detects format + stores.
Configure — choose Auto (CAIA), set constraints (max_stores, min/max OPD, max P90 time), pick a geo file, exclude stores.
Results (Run) — auto_select_stores() runs the 5-phase CAIA → stores + per-CCC assignments; optimizer does the two-pass assign + metrics.
KPIs, per-store scorecards and charts render (plotly); any Uncovered CCCs are shown, never dropped silently.
Map — build_interactive_map() draws a Leaflet map; click / bulk-select CCCs to reassign, then apply the changes.
Export — download *_optimized.xlsx (live formulas + scorecards + Uncovered CCCs) and the map HTML; save the config YAML.
Scenarios — run gap detection / placement / what-if, compare scenarios, and snapshot to history.

svg.text: Same config drives the CLI — identical results, no GUI
# my_config.yaml (the web and CLI read the same shape)
• The web pages and run.py both only collect input
and call topology_engine — zero business logic in either.
• utils/state saves uploads to a temp file so pandas sees
the exact same bytes the CLI would read.
• So a result you get in the browser matches the CLI run
of the same file + config, every time.
• CAIA never discards whole stores blindly — it moves
individual CCCs and reports whatever truly can't be served.
